subject: Quick favor
top_finding: Display name matches a protected person

message.subject: Quick favor
message.excerpt:
Hi,

Are you at your desk? I'm in a meeting and can't talk. I need you to buy gift cards for a staff appreciation surprise. It's urgent, I'll reimburse you today. Reply as soon as you see this.

Elaine

findings.title: Display name matches a protected person
evidence: Display name matches Elaine Whitfield, sent from external domain gmail[.]com
findings.lesson: Leaders get impersonated constantly. An odd request from the boss's name deserves a phone call, not a reply.

findings.title: Money request with warning signs
evidence: Money-related wording ("gift cards") combined with urgent wording
findings.lesson: Requests to move money or change bank details need a second channel. Call the person on a number you already have.

findings.title: Replies go to a different domain
evidence: From gmail[.]com but replies go to proton[.]me
findings.lesson: Look at where a reply would actually land. If it isn't the sender's own domain, the person writing may not be who they say.
